title: Yokohama Landmark Tower
visualBrief: The 1993 four-corner granite tower: gently narrowing square shaft with deep recessed ribbons, creased triangular transition panels, glazed upper hotel, projecting crown piers and a recessed mechanical roof.

nativeAxes.front: four similar faces; reconstructed symmetric entries
nativeAxes.origin: Mapped tower-only frame at reconstructed street grade

sourceFacts.architect: The Stubbins Associates and Mitsubishi Estate (now Mitsubishi Jisho Design)

reconstruction.massing: The separately mapped exact-QID tower way64891750 establishes the approximately74.9m ground envelope, excluding the adjacent mall. Mitsubishi Estate measured20F plan gives66.32m width. Original Stubbins section and architect photographs constrain the gentle taper, three transition zones and four extended corner piers.
reconstruction.facade: Individual inset horizontal glazing ribbons turn through chamfered recessed sides. Heavy granite corner piers contain small slit windows; upper hotel panes and thin white bands contrast with projecting lower office spandrels. Creased triangular folded panels stand in front of modeled horizontal louvers.
reconstruction.crown: Four L-shaped granite piers extend above the recessed central mechanical roof. Three thick horizontal bars bridge each recessed face below the tip. Small visible roof plant and antenna rods stay below the architectural crown height.
reconstruction.entry: Tower-only glazed entries and supported shallow glass canopies sit inside the mapped tower frame; the adjacent low-rise mall and separate castle-like pavilion building are not incorporated into this asset.

geometrySource: Original deterministic exterior geometry; no downloaded meshes or copied photographic textures. Footprint-derived registration includes separately attributed OpenStreetMap evidence.
sourceLicense: Original reconstruction under repository license. Map-derived plan evidence: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0. Reference publications are linked, not redistributed.
materialMethod: Canonical shared material graphs bound through molenSurface extras with metric coordinates divided by central repeat meters. Vertex colors provide component tint. Glass retains opaque metallic-roughness PBR; no bitmap texture copies per model.
reviewStatus: source-geometry; near/far and shared-material captures pending
limitations: Original93742triangles/10852416byte master remains exactly reproducible from unchanged recipe. Reviewed source retains all58 modeled ribbon floor datums, narrow pier slits, three groups of4/4/3 creased folds, recessed hotel panes, projecting granite corner crown piers and three crown bars per face, mechanical roof/plant/rods and symmetric tower-only entries. It reduces granite panel joints, seal width subdivisions, louvre repeats and tube sampling; all original small detail remains available through original recipe. The canopy now faces upward and downward explicitly. Skyline averages facade ribbons and shared graph colours into one group, retaining all folds, recessed crown and four coarse supported canopies while omitting plant/rods/fine seams/door details. District restores coarse ribbon cadence, roof equipment and reconstructed entry frames; street restores all ribbon heights with proud slit patches and planar sill trim, sparse louvres and no fold-edge tubes/door handles; close-up restores fine seals, closed sills, reveal depth, tubes and handles. Granite and coated-metal graphs approximate stone, roof concrete and stainless trim with three near draw groups, zero embedded images. Intermediate heights/fold projection, entry compass identity and plant details remain reconstructed. Finite along-ray1.5/.75/.3/.1m main-surface comparisons exclude omitted narrow trim/hardware; no global geometric-error, surveyed grade or device-performance claim.
importReason: Preserve thin facade frames, panel joints and crown/antenna details until a measured LOD chain is authored.
